findings.title: Abutting-window acceptance fixture references an undeclared window
findings.detail: The acceptance case declares windows a and c, but its first observation inherits helper default window_id w1. The implementation therefore returns UNKNOWN_WINDOW_REFERENCE before the intended non-overlap boundary is exercised, so the failing assertion is not evidence that abutting declared windows are rejected.

findings.title: Malformed None proposal is replaced by the test helper default
findings.detail: The malformed-proposal test passes None expecting INVALID_PROPOSAL, while its _prove helper also uses None to mean construct a valid default proposal. The helper silently replaces the malformed value, so the assertion does not exercise evaluate_prove with None even though the implementation rejects non-BrainProposal values.

findings.title: Malformed-window test omits constructor bounds
findings.detail: The malformed-window fixture includes the two-item tuple ("w", "TRAINING") but expands it directly into EvaluationWindow. Because start and end are omitted, Python raises TypeError before window validation can produce the expected ValueError, so the gate fails without testing invalid-role fail-closed behavior.

findings.title: PROVE candidate contaminates shared governance module identity
findings.detail: After the PROVE candidate tests are collected, existing governance tests observe two distinct ModelStatus enum classes with the same RESEARCH value: identity comparison fails and ModelRegistry.by_status returns no matching model. This proves that candidate-level module loading or cleanup changes shared atp module identity inside the pytest process, so the full deterministic suite is not isolated even though the PROVE-focused tests pass.

findings.title: Proposal created at the evaluation start is graded as prior evidence
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 shows that a proposal with created_at exactly equal to an evaluation window start is accepted, and an observation at that same instant can produce a proven result. The boundary only rejects created_at values strictly greater than the start, so the result does not prove that the proposal existed before the closed evaluation evidence began.

findings.title: Public PROVE result objects admit internally inconsistent proven totals
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 constructs public ProveMetrics, ProveEvaluation and ProveResult values whose proven aggregate reports net_return 999 while the declared window metrics sum to 0.03. Their constructors do not enforce the cross-object accounting invariant, so formally typed audit evidence can be forged outside evaluate_prove.

findings.title: Empty or cherry-picked outcome sets can still be marked proven
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 shows that empty observations and a subset omitting a losing observation can both produce proven results. The input contains no immutable expected-opportunity manifest, and observation delay is not bound to the evaluation availability interval, so the harness cannot prove that the graded rows are complete or were available only after the declared window began.

findings.title: Hostile explicit inputs can escape the refusal boundary
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 shows that a tampered gross_return of 10**5000 raises ValueError during input checksum binding before the refusal handler, while a hostile tzinfo.utcoffset raises RuntimeError during validation inside a handler that catches only _ProveError. Both explicit boundary values escape instead of producing a deterministic failed ProveResult.

findings.title: Distinct explicit inputs share the same audit checksum
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 shows identical input and refusal checksums for 0.1 versus its next representable float, for large delays differing by one microsecond, and for distinct opaque values of the same type. Pre-rounding floats, total_seconds conversion and type-only opaque canonicalization erase semantically distinct supplied input.

findings.title: Reusing the same accepted iterator changes a proven result
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 passes the same iterator object twice and obtains proven results with graded_count two and then zero because the accepted Iterable was consumed. The public boundary therefore admits an explicit input whose result depends on prior evaluation history rather than only on the supplied arguments.

findings.title: A BrainProposal subclass can override trusted audit identity
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 uses one BrainProposal subclass instance whose checksum override changes between calls. Both calls are proven with the same evaluator input checksum but different proposal and result checksums because isinstance accepts the subclass and the boundary invokes its overridable method.

findings.title: A normal rolling walk-forward schedule is rejected
findings.detail: Independent reproduction on the immutable repaired candidate reviewed in Run 31 supplies the ordered folds training-1, evaluation-1, training-2, evaluation-2. The all-to-all comparison rejects evaluation-1 because later training-2 ends after it starts, even though each evaluation follows its corresponding earlier training fold, so the harness cannot represent the rolling walk-forward objective.

findings.title: Import safety fixture rejects the annotations future directive
findings.detail: Run 32 Gate proves that the AST-based research-only import test observes only the expected safe roots plus __future__, introduced by the harmless from __future__ import annotations directive. The exact allowlist omits __future__, so the gate fails even though no trading, randomness, clock, provider or execution import is present.

findings.title: Governance identity fixture constructs the enum with the wrong value case
findings.detail: Run 32 Gate proves that the preceding module and ModelStatus identity assertion passes, but the next assertion calls ModelStatus("RESEARCH") even though the clean pinned governance enum value is "research". The resulting ValueError is a malformed test fixture and does not reproduce governance module identity contamination.

findings.title: Observation permutation changes the proof checksum
findings.detail: Run 32 Gate proves that forward and reversed observations produce different proof checksums although evaluation canonicalizes them into the same semantic outcome order. Input checksum binding encodes the original tuple order before the canonical evaluation, so equivalent observation sets have different proof identities.

findings.title: Research-only source check confuses prose with a random dependency
findings.detail: The structural safety test bans the raw substring random across the complete source text, so the harmless docstring word randomness fails the gate although the module imports only the expected standard-library and local research modules. The assertion does not distinguish executable imports or calls from documentation prose.
